clue.text: Dim thing made out when it's usually dark

indicators.note: made out suggests the letters are worked into a new form, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone peers at a faint object they can barely make out in the darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made out' signals an anagram of DIM and THING together.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of the night is the classic time of full darkness, so the phrase describes that hour.

clue.text: Italian family doctor one needed in Rome

parts.note: a medic is a doctor
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An Italian family's doctor is needed in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Medici were the ruling banking family of Renaissance Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medici were the powerful Florentine dynasty of bankers and patrons in Renaissance Italy.

clue.text: Boxer shorts, for example? People remove them after eating

definitions.meaning: a boxer is a breed of dog, so its shorts would jokily be canine trousers
containers in which diners take home leftovers from a restaurant

explanation.surface: Underwear is taken off after a large meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is old slang for trousers, so a boxer dog's shorts are a joke version.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurant containers for leftovers are named as if for the dog, and bags are also trousers.

clue.text: Fascinated by Edward, it's said, in a monotonous way

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on or fascinated by it
Ned is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone besotted with Edward speaks of him in a dull drone.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to speak or recite in a flat, chanting voice, so it describes something uttered monotonously.

clue.text: Own about a pound, split with another

indicators.note: the verb goes about, that is around, the pound

parts.note: to have something is to own it
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: Someone owns about a pound and shares it with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something into two equal parts is to share it equally with one other person.

clue.text: Get to the bottom of, or some distance down

definitions.meaning: to understand something fully, to work it out
a unit of six feet used for measuring the depth of water

explanation.surface: A diver resolves to understand the sea's depths, measuring them as they go.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means comprehend; the noun is the nautical depth measure of six feet.

clue.text: Shock about monarch turning up in this costume

indicators.note: the shock word goes about, around, the turned monarch

parts.note: to appal is to shock

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up reads the letters bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch caused shock by appearing in a strange outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's standard monarch; in a down clue 'turning up' means read upwards, and 'in this costume' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel means clothing or dress, which is what a costume is.

clue.text: Temporary problem impacted church

parts.note: something that impacted another hit it

explanation.surface: A brief problem had an effect on the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a temporary snag or difficulty that holds things up.

clue.text: Faithfully executed?

parts.note: faithfully looks like carried out loyally, but it means put to death for one's faith

explanation.surface: A task carried out with loyal care.
explanation.definitionFit: A person killed for their religious faith is a martyr, so they were executed because of faith.

clue.text: Evil spirit, maybe -—- no good could come of it

indicators.note: the answer could come out of the preceding letters once rearranged

explanation.surface: An evil spirit perhaps, from which nothing good could come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could come of it' signals an anagram of MAYBE, NO and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogeyman is an imaginary evil being used to frighten children.

clue.text: Person counting on fingers? It's much more advanced!

definitions.text: Person counting on fingers? It's much more advanced!

parts.words: Person counting on fingers? It's much more advanced!
parts.note: digits are fingers, so a person counting on them is jokily a fingers-based calculator, while the real machine is far more sophisticated

explanation.surface: A child tallies sums on their hands while a far cleverer device sits nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital machine computes with digits, which are also fingers, so the cryptic reading is a pun on that word.

clue.text: Beginnings of knowledge, say, in South American capital

indicators.note: say means the letters are spoken aloud, their names giving the sound of the answer

parts.note: the opening two letters of the word knowledge are K and N

explanation.surface: A schoolchild learns the first lessons of knowledge in a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken as letter names, K and N sound like 'kay-en'. Cayenne is the capital of French Guiana.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is the capital city of French Guiana, on the north coast of South America.

clue.text: Relating to material things no-hoper doesn't have

definitions.meaning: worldly, of this world rather than spiritual
from the British idiom 'not have an ...', meaning to have no chance at all

explanation.surface: A hopeless case lacks any connection to the material world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not an earthly' is British slang for no chance whatever, so a no-hoper hasn't got one.
explanation.definitionFit: Worldly and material things belong to this world, the opposite of heavenly; the second sense comes from the idiom of having no chance.

clue.text: Article on eccentric American mother that's spicy

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
A is the indefinite article
mom is the American spelling of mum

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a quirky American mum is rather racy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the article after CARD. 'spicy' suggests racy writing, but the answer is a spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardamom is an aromatic spice from the seeds of an Indian plant, so it is a thing that's spicy.

clue.text: Impressive joke I pocketed in coat

indicators.note: pocketed in means held inside the coat, so the joke and I go within

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: An impressive gag was tucked into the pocket of a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic means stately and grand, so it is a close synonym of impressive.

clue.text: Cryptic clue about king's wealth

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, that is around, the king
cryptic means puzzling or hidden, so the next word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A puzzling crossword clue concerns a monarch's riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' turns CLUE into LUCE; 'about' puts it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or profit, usually with a hint of disapproval, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Bat, for example, takes insect with hesitation

parts.note: a cricket is a chirping insect
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A bat catches an insect after a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' suggests the flying animal, but it is a person who bats in cricket, England's bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman is often called a bat, and one who plays the game is a player of it.

clue.text: Realise one can't stay for this meal

definitions.meaning: to put a plan into effect, accomplish it

definitions.text: one can't stay for this meal
definitions.meaning: a takeaway meal, which is taken home rather than eaten on the premises

explanation.surface: A diner realises they cannot stay to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: As a Scottish and Irish term it means a takeaway meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to perform or accomplish; the noun is a takeaway, eaten off the premises.

clue.text: Very short line finally dispatched in attack

indicators.note: the last letter is sent away, so the final L is removed

parts.note: to assail someone is to attack them
L is a common abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A very short line of troops is finally dispatched in an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally dispatched' removes the L at the end of ASSAIL. Assai is the musical term meaning 'very', as in allegro assai.
explanation.definitionFit: In musical directions the Italian word assai means very, intensifying the tempo marking.

clue.text: One, then a hundred, entered — that's not accurate

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the hundred and a are placed inside, entering the word for then

parts.note: next means then, after that
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: One person, then a hundred more, came in, which is not quite right.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise, not quite correct, so it is a synonym of not accurate.

clue.text: Nuisance addressed by solicitors

parts.note: solicitors here are those soliciting custom, who send unwanted addressed post, not lawyers

explanation.surface: A firm of lawyers is asked to handle a troublesome case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitors' suggests British lawyers, but it means people who solicit business by post.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolicited advertising post is a nuisance, and it arrives addressed by firms soliciting trade.

clue.text: Rich individual welcomed by my editor

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken inside, so the individual goes within the first word

parts.note: taken as written
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A wealthy individual was warmly received by my editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed means wealthy, having plenty of money, so it matches rich.

clue.text: President's loyal servant, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are spoken aloud, giving the surname by sound

parts.note: a true man is a faithful, loyal servant

explanation.surface: A president's faithful aide is talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry S. Truman was the 33rd US President.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Truman was President of the United States from 1945 to 1953.

clue.text: Fellow leaves those who falsify statements in news agency

indicators.note: the fellow leaves, so his letter is taken out

parts.note: refuters prove statements false, which is to falsify them

explanation.surface: A man walks out on a group of liars at a news agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falsify' looks like lying, but here it means proving false.
explanation.definitionFit: Reuters is a long-established international news agency founded in London.

clue.text: Trap in sub, endangering some inside

indicators.note: only some of the letters, taken from inside the words, give the answer

explanation.surface: A submarine is caught, endangering some of the crew inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' is the plumbing sense: the bent pipe under a sink that holds water to block smells.
explanation.definitionFit: In plumbing, a trap is the curved section of pipe that holds water to seal off drain gases.

clue.text: Name — for a girl, from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear means the word is spoken aloud and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: Monica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a name for a baby girl based on what they have heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Moniker is informal slang for a person's name or nickname.

clue.text: Hot material periodical mostly reproduced

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept
reproduced means the word is copied, so it appears twice

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical

explanation.surface: Most of a racy periodical was reprinted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduced' doubles MAG to MAGMAG; 'mostly' drops the final G.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is molten rock beneath the earth's surface, so it is extremely hot material.

clue.text: Essential software for MO?

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a method of operating, which can be expanded jokily to the core program a computer runs on

explanation.surface: A medical officer needs basic software to work.
explanation.walkthrough: MO looks like a medical officer, but read as modus operandi it is a system of operating.
explanation.definitionFit: The core software that runs a computer is literally a system for operating, matching the expansion of MO.

clue.text: Amorous American's aim, until now

definitions.meaning: an American suitor aims to go out with someone, to arrange a romantic outing
so far, up to the present

explanation.surface: An amorous American has had one aim up to now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' in the romantic sense is chiefly American usage, hence the American.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up to the present; separately, an American suitor wants to go out on an outing with someone.

clue.text: Duck and orange

definitions.meaning: a brightly coloured duck native to East Asia

explanation.surface: Duck à l'orange, a classic restaurant dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a colourful Asian duck and a small citrus fruit like a tangerine.
